name: Shakti cerebellum: modulated 40 Hz below the inion
summary: The modulated 40 Hz form of Murphy's one-coil Shakti cerebellum session: 20 min from one coil just below the bony ridge at the back of the head. The vendor lists modulated 40 Hz beside its ERP signal as a suggested signal for the cerebellum, which it says is 'considered by some to be a pleasure center', and reports no session with it there.
setting: In series that alternate with series over other areas (vendor). Sit, or lie on your side, so the coil at the back of the head is not pressed.
schedule: Vendor: alternate cerebellar series with series over other areas. The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break.
notes: The vendor's 'Cerebellum' page lists modulated 40 Hz under 'Suggested signals for the cerebellum' and says no more. Of the signal it says only 'This signal has a constant tone' ('Modulated 40 Hz Signal') and that it 'falls in and out of phase with the brain's own version'; the file is not published. Played here: a phase-modulated sine rebuilt from that description, a 40 Hz carrier whose phase swings up to 3 rad either way at 0.5 Hz (about 38.5 to 41.5 Hz), on 1-ms points. The 0.5 Hz, the 3 rad and the 20 min are the project's choice. One coil at Iz. The vendor says 'The Occipital Lobes are above the bony ridge on the back of your head. The Cerebellar vermis is just below it' ('Cerebellum'). Iz lies on the ridge and no 10-5 site lies below it, so the name is the nearest label: seat the coil just below the ridge and check that it sits firmly. Field strength: the vendor calibrates the signal at 10 mG 'when measured from one coil'. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT that is about 56 uT (560 mG) at the coil face, 56 times the vendor's figure. Under the neck muscles the cerebellum lies deeper than 20 mm; by the coil model the field at 40 mm is about a sixth of that at 20 mm. No report of this session exists: the vendor says the signal 'has been used by only four people' (FAQ) and 'you should consider it as an untested signal'. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Gendle & McGrath tested the amygdala signal, not this one. The ERP form is murphy-shakti-cerebellum-erp. The vendor warns that 'excess cerebellar activation may lead to emotional flattening', so do not overuse it. Not for people with epilepsy; stop if distressed.
